performance.what_the_data_shows:
What the data shows
- Mobile paint metrics are consistently strong across the site: average FCP ~1206 ms and average LCP ~1236 ms.
- Mobile interactivity is the main constraint: average Total Blocking Time (TBT) ~403.5 ms (with one URL far higher), indicating JavaScript and main-thread work are delaying responsiveness.
- Page weight is moderate-to-high and skewed toward images and scripts: average total transfer ~2.19 MB; images ~1.39 MB; scripts ~0.73 MB; third-party ~0.48 MB.
- Server latency is not the primary bottleneck but is non-trivial: average ~331 ms on mobile and ~402 ms on desktop, with some third-party origins (notably Instagram) slower than the first-party origin.
- Desktop results are generally excellent for interactivity: average TBT ~3.7 ms, and lower main-thread work (~533 ms), suggesting mobile CPU constraints amplify the cost of current JavaScript and rendering work.
performance.key_strengths:
Key strengths
- Fast first paint and largest paint on both devices (site averages: mobile FCP/LCP ~1.2 s; desktop FCP ~0.56 s, LCP ~0.98 s).
- Low desktop blocking time (TBT ~3.7 ms average), indicating good baseline runtime performance on stronger devices.
- Reasonable request counts on average (32.4 requests), with a high proportion of successful responses (30.4 200s on average; ~2 non-200s).
- CSS and document transfer sizes are relatively small compared to images/scripts (avg CSS ~44 KB; avg document ~23 KB), reducing render-blocking pressure from these resource types.
performance.primary_weaknesses:
Primary weaknesses
- Elevated mobile TBT (~403.5 ms average) suggests too much main-thread work before the page becomes reliably responsive; the worst page reaches ~887.5 ms TBT.
- Main-thread work composition indicates time spent in "Other" and rendering/layout/script evaluation (mobile average main-thread work ~2396 ms; with large contributions from Other ~1200 ms and paint/composite/render ~732 ms).
- Heavy images dominate transfer on key pages (e.g., homepage ~3.13 MB images of ~3.77 MB total), increasing download/decoding work and memory pressure on mobile.
- Large and recurring JavaScript payloads on service/about pages (e.g., a ~309 KB transfer JS bundle with ~1,030,665 bytes resource size) combined with high third-party transfer on /about (~1.25 MB) increase parse/eval and network overhead.
- Non-200 responses occur consistently (2 per URL), which can create wasted work and latency even when UX metrics look good.
performance.high_level_roadmap:
High level roadmap
- Phase 1 (high impact, lowest risk): Reduce mobile main-thread blocking
- Break up and defer non-critical JavaScript on pages with high TBT (prioritise /services/social-media-management and the homepage).
- Audit long tasks (high task counts on some pages, e.g., homepage ~5878) and reduce work in "Other" and rendering/layout buckets by removing non-essential runtime work and simplifying above-the-fold UI.
- Phase 2 (high impact): Reduce image transfer and decoding costs
- Target the largest images by transfer size (e.g., ~810 KB and ~646 KB testimonial PNGs on the homepage; ~553 KB JPEGs used across pages). Resize/compress to the displayed dimensions and prefer more efficient formats where feasible.
- Ensure below-the-fold images are not competing with critical resources (prioritise hero/above-the-fold images, deprioritise the rest).
- Phase 3 (medium impact): Control third-party overhead and latency variance
- Reduce or delay third-party resources where transfer size is high (notably /about with ~1.25 MB third-party transfer) and where server response times are slower (Instagram origins).
- Phase 4 (ongoing): Hygiene and stability
- Investigate and eliminate recurring non-200 requests (average ~2 per page) to reduce retries/failures and ensure consistent loading behavior.

prioritisation_method: Prioritised by (1) user-perceived impact on mobile responsiveness and load (TBT, main-thread work, transfer size), (2) frequency across URLs (repeated large assets/bundles and consistent non-200 responses), and (3) implementation effort (quick wins first: image optimization and deferral/cleanup before deeper architectural changes). SEO items are deprioritised because there are zero failures in the provided data.
